title: The Failure Mechanism: How to Make It Work for You Instead of Against You
coreMove: Treat FAILURE signals like a fever: name the unwanted direction, refuse the identity label, and take one corrective action before the symptom becomes a self-portrait.

exampleSpecs.audience: readers who treat bad moods as identity proof
exampleSpecs.stakes: A warning sign may become shame instead of corrective action.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use the fever comparison to turn a bad feeling into a corrective cue.

exampleSpecs.audience: teams confusing effort with effective correction
exampleSpecs.stakes: More pressure on a futile method can damage morale and still miss the goal.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show frustration turning from extra force into a change of method.

exampleSpecs.audience: people who fear their anger will either leak out or explode
exampleSpecs.stakes: Aggressive energy may wreck a working relationship if it has no safe outlet.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use an unsent anger letter and burning it to redirect steam.

exampleSpecs.audience: makers who withdraw when rough work feels like self-exposure
exampleSpecs.stakes: Avoiding contact can deepen Insecurity and Loneliness while the skill stays stuck.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Turn the FAILURE acronym into a check before withdrawal becomes the answer.

exampleSpecs.audience: operators who delay action until certainty feels complete
exampleSpecs.stakes: No movement means the system receives no steering data.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show uncertainty blocking correction until a small test creates feedback.

exampleSpecs.audience: readers who confuse low demand with real peace
exampleSpecs.stakes: A life without strain may also lose the goal that gives energy a direction.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Read emptiness as a call for a worthwhile target rather than more withdrawal.
